caption: A rubber ball rolls across a polished wooden floor onto a thick shaggy rug and comes to a stop on the rug.

sa.check: A rubber ball rolls across a polished wooden floor.
It runs onto a thick shaggy rug.
It comes to a stop on the rug.
The change of surface from bare wood to rug is visible.
The roll on the wood comes first, then the rug, then the stop.

pc.expect: The ball rolls freely on the wood, and the marked slowing starts where it reaches the rug, ending in a stop a short way onto it.
pc.fail: The ball comes to a stop on the bare wood with nothing in its way; or it crosses onto the rug without slowing at all; or it slows on the rug and then rolls on quicker again.

pc.expect: The ball keeps a straight line and stays at rest once it has stopped.
pc.fail: The ball curves on the open floor with nothing touching it; or it gathers speed on the rug; or it sets off again after coming to rest.

pc.expect: The ball stays down on the floor and on top of the rug throughout.
pc.fail: The ball lifts off the floor and travels through the air; or it hovers above the pile of the rug; or it sinks into the floorboards.

pc.expect: The shaggy pile is pressed down under the ball and springs back, while the ball stays round and firm.
pc.fail: The rug's pile stays undisturbed where the ball plainly rolls over it; or the rug ripples like water right across the room; or the ball squashes into the pile and stays flattened.

pc.expect: One ball, one rug and one floor are there throughout.
pc.fail: The ball vanishes at the edge of the rug or a second one appears; or the ball passes through the rug to the floor beneath; or the rug turns into another object.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The ball's colour, the rug's pattern and the room stay the same.
pc.fail: The ball changes colour as it rolls; or the rug changes pattern or size between frames; or the room behind rearranges.
